digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and ticket digest history management
propositions: File deletion does not reclaim git repository space; the 1.02 GiB pack retains all blobs regardless of 3,200 historical deletes, making physical prune a cost without benefit for clone/fetch size.

Queue reduction read cost is O(history) for current _events_of implementation which opens all matching files; suffix-lazy reading of newest-first dirents reduces file opens from 4,977 to 1,658 per full-store scan without changing tree semantics.

The enrich drain gate check currently takes 404-692 ms against a 20 ms budget, primarily due to listdir and open calls across 3,727 ticket dirs; read-bound design fixes the unbounded opens term but not the listdir constant.
Merge-safe retention schemes must rename to deterministic source-derived paths with identical content; deletion paired with UUID add creates rename/rename conflicts across clones.

Bounding reads via newest-first suffix scan preserves every committed UUID event and does not alter tree structure or merge semantics, making it merge-safe by construction without requiring I1 amendment.
